candidates.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
candidates.content: We present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing a perception layer for agents that read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities. Its design rests on one encoder for every modality and one schema for every task. Youtu-Omni-Encoder, initialized from a pre-trained language model to strengthen text reading, encodes all modalities with shared weights in a unified space-time coordinate system, and a few fusion layers let video frames attend to concurrent audio, bringing cross-modal fusion and temporal alignment into perception itself. OmniSchema unifies the outputs of all ten parsing tasks, allowing a single self-evolving post-training procedure, OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation (OSAD), to provide a shared token-role-based objective across tasks. In each round, the model is trained on its own rollouts against token-level targets from a reference-conditioned copy of itself, which is then refreshed with the trained weights, so that the parser and its supervision co-evolve. candidates.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
candidates.content: Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. Endowing aerial robots with an analogous functional organization remains challenging, as existing systems are often specialized for individual capabilities, dependent on offboard computation, or unable to sustain closed-loop operation on resource-constrained platforms. We present OpenFlyV2, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model. A compact action expert converts the shared multimodal context into short-horizon flight waypoints, while motion-aware temporal memory and action priors reduce the computational cost of closed-loop execution. We construct , a simulation-based dataset comprising approximately 70,000 navigation trajectories and 60,000 vision-language instruction--response pairs. candidates.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions
candidates.content: We present PhysInsert, a framework for physically plausible reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and their surrounding scenes. Existing methods often rely on masked inputs, generation-based pairs, or training pairs with limited viewpoint variation, leaving pose and illumination adaptation and bidirectional object-scene interactions insufficiently constrained. We construct the Insert World dataset with strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs and object references across viewpoints and lighting conditions. Building on these data, Geometry-Guided Adaptation couples a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams under target-scene feature supervision to guide spatially consistent insertion. Complementary 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision jointly supervises object occupancy and environmental changes while grounding spatial instructions in object regions through image-text attention. We introduce PhysInsert-Bench with dedicated cross-environment and cross-view cases requiring illumination and pose adaptation beyond appearance copying. candidates.title: Quoting Terk Terkowitz
candidates.content: If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for. — Terk Terkowitz , An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI Tags: amazon , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , ai , llms

candidates.title: Intradermal Influenza Vaccination- Healthy Cohort
candidates.content: [EARLY_PHASE1] COMPLETED | 申办方/赞助方: Yale University | 适应症: Vaccine Reaction. The goal of this study is to characterize the immune response, both innate and adaptive, as well as locally and systemic, to intradermal (ID) vaccination in healthy individuals compared to intramuscular vaccination and placebo. The intervention involves intradermal administration of an FDA-approved intramuscular seasonal influenza vaccine, using an FDA-approved device MicronJet. Investigators will measure antibody titers, cell subtypes, and multi-omic profiles, by collecting skin and peripheral blood at baseline and at several time points after vaccination. The primary objective is to identify baseline correlates of immune response in the skin and peripheral blood to the seasonal influenza vaccine. The investigators secondary goals are to describe the inflammatory response in the skin over time.

candidates.title: PREVENT HPV -Related Cancers Trial
candidates.content: [PHASE3] ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: University of Utah | 适应症: HPV Vaccination, Uptake Vaccination, Series Completion. This study will serve as one of the first to develop and test the effectiveness of strategies to promote HPV vaccination among diverse rural parents and caregivers of children ages 9-17 years in the Mountain West. Once implemented into practice, our intervention could significantly reduce disparities in the burden of HPV-associated cancers among rural populations in the United States. The proposed study will assess the effectiveness of a clinic-based behavioral outreach intervention to increase HPV vaccination rates at community clinics in rural counties. The intervention consists of communication and engagement strategies delivered within routine care settings and is designed to pose no more than minimal risk to participants.

candidates.title: Culturally Targeted Health Communication and Receptivity to the Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Among Parents in Flint, MI
candidates.content: [NA] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Michigan State University | 适应症: HPV Vaccination. The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if culturally targeted messaging about the human papillomavirus (HPV) increases receptivity to the HPV vaccine among African American parents of vaccine-eligible daughters. The main question it aims to answer is: • Does culturally targeted messaging increase African American parents' intentions to vaccinate their daughter against HPV? Research will compare culturally targeted messaging to general, educational messaging and no messaging. Participants will: * View culturally targeted messages, education-only messages, or no messages about the HPV vaccine * Report their intentions to vaccinate their daughter against HPV * Report whether they have initiated HPV vaccination for their daughter six months later

candidates.title: The Physician of The Future
candidates.content: In the midst of the present social upheaval, one may well wonder the position physicians will eventually occupy in the cosmic scheme. Intelligent observers inform us that the answer depends entirely on our own conduct—the mass conduct inherent in intelligent organization. If physicians are to assume that leadership essential to sane medical progress, they must evolve an outline of purposes, a constructive forward-looking program of things to be done, of channels through which cooperation must flow toward their leadership. This constructive program must be so wisely planned and so faithfully followed by all worth-while physicians that at least the intelligent element of public opinion will go with it.

candidates.title: Diagnostic Delays Associated With a Screening Trial of a Multicancer Early Detection Test—Reply
candidates.content: In Reply We appreciate Dr Froehner’s thoughtful comments on our article reporting differentially higher diagnostic delay rates in regions participating in a population-based cell-free DNA–based MCED trial. As Dr Froehner notes, many health conditions are associated with poverty, as in the case of the lung, head and neck, and upper gastrointestinal cancers that we focused on in our study. Long-standing disparities in who receives preventive care, screening tests, and diagnostic follow-up contribute to these inequities.

candidates.title: [Series] A global men's health epidemiology within an intersectional framework
candidates.content: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990–2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes.

candidates.title: [Series] Charting a course to men's health and wellbeing: applying a lens of power and politics to improve men's health outcomes
candidates.content: Despite long-standing evidence of poor health and life expectancy outcomes among men, particularly among men who are socially or structurally marginalised, men's health has generally received little and uneven attention in health policy and practice. Its gendered and intersectional aspects have been especially overlooked. This third paper in the Lancet Men's Health Series examines why men's health has received so little policy attention and proposes strategies to raise men's health on national and global agendas.

candidates.title: A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2hi Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease

Pedersen et al. define the phenotypic diversity of human CD4+ T cells recognizing a defined Bacteroidales epitope across disease settings. This revealed a TMIGD2hi Th17 phenotype that expands in inflamed tissue. More broadly, this work underscores the malleability of microbiota-specific T cells during inflammatory bowel disease.

The authors concluded that this delay is unlikely to materially influence the interpretation of trial results.

candidates.title: [Perspectives] Derek Griffith: transformative leader in men's health
candidates.content: “We know a lot about male health. We don’t know a lot about men's health”, says Derek Griffith, who is one of the authors of a new Lancet Series on men's health. “Male health is about male bodies and hormones. Men's health is more holistic and comprehensive and should consider psychological, social, and structural factors like race, ethnicity, country of origin, and colonisation, which a biomedical approach has largely missed.”

candidates.title: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis
candidates.content: Hundreds to thousands of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10–20 μm in size) move up to hundreds of micrometers inside the tissue of their acoel worm hosts (Waminoa sp., millimeters in size). Host actin machinery is primarily responsible for driving symbiont mobility at speeds around 1 μm/s, and symbionts move inside ribbon-like host cells (∼200 nm thin), which stretch to accommodate symbionts moving through them.

candidates.title: The 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein links the cell responses to transcription and replication stress by promoting replication fork reversal and homologous recombination
candidates.content: Abstract The 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK-snRNP) releases positive transcription elongation factor b to sustain RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) activity during transcription stress. Many conditions that block transcription also cause replication stress, and 7SK-snRNP components have potential roles in transcription–replication conflicts and double-strand break (DSB) repair. Here, we investigate roles of 7SK-snRNP components in replication stress responses. We report that 7SK-snRNP promotes replication fork slowing in response to agents that cause both replication and transcription stress. Our data suggest that 7SK-snRNP facilitates RAD51-mediated replication fork reversal rather than transcription–replication conflicts. 7SK-snRNP also promotes RAD51 recruitment to replication-associated DSBs or post-replicative gaps under conditions of transcription stress and supports homologous recombination at direct DSBs. In contrast, 7SK-snRNP components are not required for RAD51 recruitment in response to hydroxyurea. candidates.title: Exploring DNA movement through the application of droplet-based high-efficiency chromatin conformation capture (DropHiChew) and loop velocity
candidates.content: Abstract This study presents a novel approach to understanding DNA movement dynamics. Chromatin conformation plays a crucial role in controlling gene expression and cellular processes, with abnormalities linked to diseases like cancer and genetic disorders. ​Current single-cell chromatin conformation methods face limitations in cost-effectiveness, accessibility, and capturing dynamic genome architecture.​​ Therefore, we develop ​DropHiChew, a droplet-based, highly efficient chromatin conformation capture method employing 10× Genomics single-cell systems for user-friendly, cost-effective implementation. Combined with our ​loop velocity algorithm—which estimates the speed and direction of cell development by quantifying chromatin movement—this approach accurately gauges the trajectory of DNA motion and cellular states even at shallow sequencing depth (50k contacts per cell). Validation demonstrates its applicability across biological systems, including HEK293T, spermiogenesis, and embryonic development. The integration of DropHiChew and loop velocity offers potential for diverse applications in chromatin capture studies. This paradigm provides a dynamic perspective on genome organiza

candidates.title: DNA defense systems become a fitness liability during plasmid conjugation
candidates.content: Abstract Horizontal gene transfer via conjugative plasmids is a major driver of bacterial evolution. While antibiotic exposure selects for the resistance genes carried by some plasmids, much uncertainty remains about how plasmids persist and spread in microbial communities in the absence of such external selection. Here, we show that conjugative plasmid transfer selectively reduces the fitness of non-permissive recipients through the process of lethal zygosis: a phenomenon in which repeated Type IV Secretion System (T4SS) engagement damages recipients that fail to establish the plasmid. We found that this contact-dependent antagonism effectively clears a niche for plasmid donors by turning recipients’ DNA defenses into a liability. Blocking establishment of the plasmid RK2 with CRISPR–Cas or restriction-modification caused strong fitness defects in Escherichia coli recipients by preventing expression of plasmid-encoded exclusion genes and leaving cells exposed to repeated T4SS engagement.
